import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_79/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_79/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# According to operation history:
# 1) JOIN Source0 and Source1 on 'city' was done, but final better result is from grouping Source1 only.
# 2) Group by Source1.city and average Source1.fare.

# So we directly group Source1 by city and average fare
target = source1.groupby('city', as_index=False)['fare'].mean()

# Ensure the schema matches target schema: ['city': string, 'fare': float]
target['city'] = target['city'].astype(str)
target['fare'] = target['fare'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the specified path
target.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city column (inner join to avoid extra rows)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', left_on='city', right_on='city')

# Group by city and aggregate average fare
result = joined.groupby('city', as_index=False).agg({'fare': 'mean'})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
